songs.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I threw the whole kitchen window open wide this morning,
the old curtains caught a warmer breath of air at last.
Winter's heavy coats all went back into the crowded closet,
the old porch chair waited empty, sitting quietly there.
I stood a long minute quiet in the open doorway,
just breathing in something new and rare and bare.

[Chorus]
Let the House Breathe,
open every single window wide, all at once.
Whatever heavy weight the long winter left upon us,
today we're finally setting it all aside.

[Verse 2]
The old garden hose still coiled up since last autumn,
I dragged it out slow to test its gentle spray.
The neighbor's kids were already out there loudly shouting,
bikes and colored chalk lines scattered down the way.
I hung the whole wash out on the line together,
first time now since a much colder day.

[Chorus]
Let the House Breathe,
open every single window wide, all at once.
Whatever heavy weight the long winter left upon us,
today we're finally setting it all aside.

[Breakdown]
The whole quiet street smells like something slowly, gently turning,
soft and green and wide awake again at last.

[Final Chorus]
Let the House Breathe,
open every single window wide, all at once.
Whatever heavy weight the long winter left upon us,
Let the House Breathe.
